chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Mahzam, from Anbasa al-Abid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Advise me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Prepare your apparatus and send forward your provision, and be your own executor, and do not say to others that they should send to you with what is adequate for you.'

key_terms.زَادُكَ: Your provision (good deeds for the journey)
key_terms.وَصِيَّ نَفْسِكَ: Executor of your own self (taking responsibility for one's soul)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be your own executor in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs Aban al-‘Abid to prepare his spiritual 'apparatus' and send forward his 'provision' (sadaqah and good deeds) as a precursor to death, emphasizing proactive self-accountability. This advice underscores the Shia concept of *tadbir* (spiritual management) and the necessity of actively cultivating one's own rectification rather than relying on others for salvation. It serves as a practical reminder that spiritual readiness is an individual duty requiring continuous effort and foresight.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibrahim Bin Mahzam, from Anbasa Al Aabid who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Advise me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Prepare your apparatus and send forward your provision, and be your own executor, and do not say to others that they should send to you with what is adequate for you’.
en.sarwar: 29. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibrahim ibn Mehzam from ‘Anbasah al-‘Abid who has narrated the following: “

I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, to give me an advice. He (the Imam) said, ‘Prepare your supplies, send them ahead of you, be the executor of your own will and do not say to others to send for you what is good for your well-being. 5 ”
